entries.test: Whether major outlets (e.g., WSJ, Technology Review) ran a series of critical stories about Altman and OpenAI in the weeks before June 4, 2024.
entries.note: The post itself lists several such stories. The plain reading is a steady run of recent negative coverage.

entries.test: Whether any model released between August 2022 and June 2024 was widely judged a leap over GPT-4 comparable to GPT-3.5→GPT-4 on benchmarks, and reported industry investment in frontier models over that period exceeding $50B.
entries.note: 'GPT-4-sized breakthrough' is loose, but benchmark comparisons give a common reading. The no-solution part is recorded as a separate claim.

entries.test: Whether, as of June 2024, leading LLMs still showed substantial hallucination, unreliability, and reasoning failures in published evaluations, and whether alignment was still regarded as unsolved.
entries.note: The post says 'the field', not 'LLMs', but the scope is effectively the same.

The quoted words are Mims's, and Marcus hedges that they echo 'a lot of' what he has 'largely' argued, so full endorsement overstates him. 'Usefulness is limited' and 'pace is slowing' have no shared test.
This is a sign-off wish, so it is normative, not rhetoric. The proposition adds a firmer factual claim that AI is 'driven more by money' than by research, which he does not state.
